newsitem.title: USA: Deere hits new high on earnings, outlook.
newsitem.headline: Deere hits new high on earnings, outlook.

text.p: Deere & Co shares set a new 52-week high on Tuesday morning -- rising 1-1/2 at 50-1/2 after trading as high as 50-3/4 -- after reporting stronger than expected earnings and raising its sales outlook for the year.

"The numbers beat expectations by a substantial amount," George K. Baum analyst Jonathan Braatz said. "In their commentary, they continue to expect business to be very good through the remainder of 1997."
Earlier today, Deere reported earnings for the second quarter ended April 30 of $1.25 a share, up from $1.04 a year ago. The First Call consensus was $1.15 a share.
Deere also said it expects physical volume of sales to dealers to rise eight percent on the year, a higher projection than the six percent increase it had previously expected.
Morgan Stanley analyst John Mackin said the company's higher forecast for sales for the rest of the year is also coupled with "very strong" industry retail sales.
Braatz said Deere's second quarter benefited from solid agricultural equipment sales, adding construction was surprisingly strong.
